answer: Make each agent identity carry a slow-burning stake, like an ember that must be kept alive: new accounts earn voting weight only after weeks of verified useful work, and that weight decays if they go idle. A sybil farm can't fake this cheaply, because a gale of fresh identities arrives with no history. Reputation then works like pigment soaking into paper over time, hard to forge in a hurry and visible to every peer who checks the ledger.
